extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Letters in Mathematical Physics (mathematical physicists/mathematicians)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting research manuscripts (including figures, data, ethics, authorship, and LaTeX/source files) to the journal Letters in Mathematical Physics published by Springer Nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and simultaneous_submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies: that the work described has not been published before; that it is not under consideration for publication anywhere else; that its publication has been approved by all co-authors, if any, as well as by the responsible authorities at the institute where the work has been carried out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher will not be held legally responsible for claims. Authors should not submit the same manuscript to multiple journals; concurrent or secondary publication is sometimes justifiable only under certain conditions (e.g., translations) which should be transparent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions for previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors wishing to include figures, tables, or text passages that have already been published elsewhere are required to obtain permission from the copyright owner(s) for both the print and online format and to include evidence that such permission has been granted when submitting their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material received without such evidence will be assumed to originate from the authors. Be aware some publishers do not grant electronic rights for free and Springer cannot refund permission costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online_submission_procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please follow the hyperlink 'Submit manuscript' and upload all of your manuscript files following the instructions given on the screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All source files you upload will be compiled into a single PDF for your approval. While the compiled PDF will be used for peer-review, the uploaded source files are transferred for publication upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision_of_editable_source_files
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure you provide all relevant editable source files at every submission and revision. Failing to submit a complete set of editable source files will result in your article not being considered for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For manuscript text submit common formats such as .docx or LaTeX. Important note: Submissions should not only consist of a pdf-file, but of the Latex-source as well! Do not use subfolders for LaTeX submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title_page_content
rubrics_metrics.description: The title page should contain: Title (concise and informative); name(s) of the author(s); affiliation(s) including institution, (department), city, (state), country; a clear indication and an active e-mail address of the corresponding author; if available, the 16-digit ORCID of the author(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If authors are unaffiliated, only city and country are captured. Address info with affiliation will be published. Acknowledgments of people, grants, funds, etc. should be placed in a separate section on the title page; funding organizations should be written in full.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large_language_models_and_authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Language Models (LLMs), such as ChatGPT, do not currently satisfy our authorship criteria. Use of an LLM should be properly documented in the Methods section (or suitable alternative) of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI-assisted copy editing (readability/style/grammar corrections) does not need to be declared; generative editorial work and autonomous content creation do. There must be human accountability for the final version and agreement from the authors that edits reflect their original work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract_requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide an abstract of 150 to 250 words. The abstract should not contain any undefined abbreviations or unspecified references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For life science journals (when applicable) include trial registration numbers and dates per instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Please provide 4 to 6 keywords which can be used for indexing purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements_and_declarations_required
rubrics_metrics.description: The following statements should be included under the heading 'Statements and Declarations' for inclusion in the published paper. Submissions that do not include relevant declarations will be returned as incomplete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes Competing Interests, Funding, Ethics approval, Consent, Data/Material/Code availability, Authors' contribution statements; sample wording and examples are provided and should be customized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript_format_LaTeX_and_templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted in LaTeX. We recommend using Springer Nature’s LaTeX template. The submission should include the original source (including all style files and figures) and a PDF version of the compiled output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All source files uploaded will be compiled into a single PDF. Further tips available on Springer LaTeX Support hub. Do not use subfolders for figures or bibliographic files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heading_structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the decimal system of headings with no more than three levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations_policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Abbreviations should be defined at first mention and used consistently thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes_rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes can be used to give additional information, which may include the citation of a reference included in the reference list. They should not consist solely of a reference citation, and they should never include the bibliographic details of a reference. They should also not contain any figures or tables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnotes to the text are numbered consecutively; those to tables by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values). Footnotes to the title or authors are not given reference symbols. Always use footnotes instead of endnotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical_statement_format
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements should preferably be set out as Theorems, Propositions, Lemmas, Definitions, etc. An introduction placing the subject in a broader context is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference_citation_style
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference citations in the text should be identified by numbers in square brackets (e.g., [1], [1-3, 7]). The reference list should only include works that are cited in the text and that have been published or accepted for publication; personal communications and unpublished works should only be mentioned in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries in the reference list should be given in alphabetic order. If available, always include DOIs as full DOI links. Use standard journal abbreviations according to ISSN LTWA; if unsure use full journal title. Examples provided for journal article, article by DOI, book, book chapter, online document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables_format_and_citation
rubrics_metrics.description: All tables are to be numbered using Arabic numerals. Tables should always be cited in text in consecutive numerical order. For each table, supply a table caption explaining the components of the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any previously published material by giving the original source in the form of a reference at the end of the table caption. Footnotes to tables should be indicated by superscript lower-case letters (or asterisks for significance values) and included beneath the table body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic_figure_submission_formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Supply all figures electronically. Indicate what graphics program was used to create the artwork. For vector graphics the preferred format is EPS; for halftones use TIFF. MSOffice files are also acceptable. Vector graphics containing fonts must have the fonts embedded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name files 'Fig' and the figure number (e.g., Fig1.eps). Do not use faint lines/lettering; ensure legibility at final size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line_art_requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Line Art: Black and white graphic with no shading. All lines should be at least 0.1 mm (0.3 pt) wide. Scanned or bitmap line drawings should have a minimum resolution of 1200 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vector graphics with fonts must have fonts embedded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Halftone_and_combination_art_resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Halftones (photographs, drawings with fine shading) should have minimum resolution of 300 dpi. Combination artwork (halftone + line art) should have minimum resolution of 600 dpi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If magnification used in photographs, indicate with scale bars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color_art_and_contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: Color art is free of charge for online publication. If black and white will be shown in the print version, make sure main information remains visible when converted to black and white.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check xerographic copy to ensure distinctions; if print will be black and white, do not refer to color in captions. Color illustrations should be submitted as RGB (8 bits per channel). Figure lettering must have contrast ratio at least 4.5:1 for accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure_lettering_and_style
rubrics_metrics.description: To add lettering use Helvetica or Arial (sans serif). Keep lettering consistently sized throughout final-sized artwork, usually about 2–3 mm (8–12 pt). Avoid effects such as shading or outline letters. Do not include titles or captions within illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variance of type size within an illustration should be minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure_numbering_captions_and_parts
rubrics_metrics.description: All figures are to be numbered using Arabic numerals and cited in text in consecutive order. Figure parts should be denoted by lowercase letters (a, b, c, etc.). Each figure should have a concise caption describing accurately what the figure depicts. Figure captions begin with the term 'Fig.' in bold type, followed by the figure number in bold; no punctuation after the number or at the end of the caption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify all elements found in the figure; identify previously published material by citation at end of caption. If appendix contains figures continue main text numbering; figures in online appendices (SI) should be numbered separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure_placement_and_size
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures should be submitted within the body of the text. Size figures to fit in the column width. For large-sized journals figures should be 84 mm (double-column) or 174 mm (single-column) wide and not higher than 234 mm; for small-sized journals 119 mm wide and not higher than 195 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If file size causes upload problems, submit large figures separately from text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure_accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To give people of all abilities access to figure content make sure: all figures have descriptive captions; patterns are used instead of or in addition to colors; any figure lettering has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative_AI_images_policy_for_figures_and_SI
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must check Springer’s policy on generative AI images and make sure work adheres to the principles described therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies both to figures and Supplementary Information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary_information_submission_and_formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Springer accepts electronic multimedia files and other supplementary files to be published online along with an article. Supply supplementary material in standard file formats and include article title, journal name, author names, affiliation and e-mail of corresponding author in each file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Larger files may require long download times. Specialized formats (e.g., .pdb, .wrl, .nb) can be supplied. Multiple files can be collected in .zip or .gz. Text/presentations should be PDF; spreadsheets .csv or .xlsx.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary_information_naming_and_citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The text must make specific mention of supplementary material as a citation similar to figures and tables. Refer to supplementary files as 'Online Resource' and name files consecutively (e.g., 'ESM_3.mpg').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each supplementary material supply a concise caption describing the content. SI will be published as received without conversion or reformatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary_accessibility_and_video_requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure manuscript contains descriptive captions for each supplementary material. Video files must not contain anything that flashes more than three times per second (to avoid risk to seizure-prone users).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audio/video/animations: aspect ratio 16:9 or 4:3; maximum file size 2 GB; minimum video duration 1 sec; supported formats listed (avi, wmv, mp4, mov, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: After_acceptance_production_and_proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon acceptance the article will be exported to Production for typesetting. You will receive an email to confirm affiliation, choose publishing model, arrange rights and payment, and a second email with a link to proofs once typesetting is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose of proofs is to check typesetting/conversion errors and completeness/accuracy of text, tables and figures. Substantial changes (new results, corrected values, title, authorship) are not allowed without editor approval. After online publication further changes require an Erratum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article_publishing_agreement_and_open_choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Depending on journal ownership/policies you will either grant the Publisher an exclusive licence to publish the article or be asked to transfer copyright. Open Choice allows publishing open access under Creative Commons license; APCs vary by journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open Choice benefits: increased visibility and easier compliance with funder mandates. Details on fees, funding and licences on the journal's Open access publishing page.

rubrics_metrics.name: MSC_classification_codes
rubrics_metrics.description: An appropriate number of MSC (Mathematics Subject Classification) codes should be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MSC is used by Mathematical Reviews and Zentralblatt MATH; see www.ams.org/msc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific_style_and_notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use internationally accepted signs and symbols for units (SI units). Use standard mathematical notation: italic for single letters denoting constants, variables, unknowns; Roman/upright for numerals, operators, punctuation, and commonly defined functions/abbreviations (e.g., cos, det, e, exp, lim, log); Bold for vectors, tensors, matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research_data_policy_and_data_availability_statement
rubrics_metrics.description: This journal follows Springer Nature research data policy. Sharing of all relevant research data is strongly encouraged and authors must add a Data Availability Statement to original research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data includes spreadsheets, images, textual extracts, archival documents, video/audio, interview notes, specialist formats. The statement should explain how to access data supporting results, include links/ citations to publicly archived datasets, or explain access conditions if not publicly shareable. Authors are encouraged to deposit data in repositories and to cite datasets with persistent identifiers (DOI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data_citation_and_repository_guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are strongly encouraged to deposit supporting data in publicly available repositories and to cite any publicly available data on which conclusions rely. Data citations should include a persistent identifier and follow DataCite minimum information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend discipline-specific repositories where available. For some data types repository submission is mandatory. Encourage open licences that permit reuse; ensure authors have rights to share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data_and_peer_review_anonymisation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the journal uses double-anonymous peer review and authors provide reviewers with access to data, it is strongly suggested that the authorship in the data is also anonymised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are repositories that can assist or create a link to mask authorship of your data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical_responsibilities_and_conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is committed to upholding integrity and follows COPE guidelines. Authors should refrain from misrepresenting research results and follow rules of good scientific practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes not submitting to more than one journal, not salami-slicing, presenting results honestly with no fabrication/falsification or inappropriate data/image manipulation, securing permissions for third-party material, avoiding plagiarism, citing appropriate literature, avoiding untrue statements about entities, identifying dual-use risks, ensuring correct authorship and order at submission, and being prepared to send raw data on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation_and_consequences_for_misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is suspicion of misbehavior or alleged fraud the Journal/Publisher will investigate following COPE. If valid concerns remain, authors will be contacted and given opportunity to respond. Possible measures include rejection, erratum/correction, expression of concern, or retraction. The author’s institution may be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retraction means article is maintained on platform, watermarked 'retracted' and explanation linked. A notice of suspected transgression may be included in bibliographic record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction_of_fundamental_errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors have an obligation to correct mistakes once they discover a significant error or inaccuracy in their published article. Contact the journal and explain how the error impacts the article. A decision on correction or retraction will depend on the nature of the error and the retraction note should provide transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggesting_or_excluding_reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are welcome to suggest suitable reviewers and/or request exclusion of certain individuals. When suggesting reviewers, ensure they are totally independent and not connected to the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend a mix of reviewers from different countries and institutions. Provide institutional email for each suggested reviewer or other verification (homepage, publication record, researcher ID). The Journal may not use suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing_interests_disclosure_scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are requested to disclose interests that are directly or indirectly related to the work submitted. Interests within the last 3 years of beginning the work should be reported; interests outside 3 years must be disclosed if they could reasonably be perceived as influencing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure aims to provide transparency and help readers judge potential bias. This is not intended to imply that financial relationships are inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples_of_competing_interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Interests to consider and disclose include: Funding (grants, support), Employment (recent/present/anticipated), Financial interests (stocks, consultancy, patents), Non-financial interests (positions on editorial/ advisory boards, consulting for educational purposes, expert witness, mentoring relationships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary research and review articles require disclosure statements. Other article types may require disclosures depending on content. Funding information should be disclosed in submission system and included in 'Declarations' section before references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary_declarations_section_and_sample_wording
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize funding and competing interests in a 'Declarations' section before the reference list under 'Funding' and/or 'Competing interests'. Examples of statements are provided for funded, no funding, and interests-to-declare cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When all authors have same/no conflicts a single blanket statement is sufficient. Authors are responsible for correctness of statements; Editor-in-Chief may reject submissions that do not meet these guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship_principles_and_recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommended authorship criteria (adapted from ICMJE): authors whose names appear should (1) make substantial contributions to conception/design, data acquisition/analysis/interpretation or software creation; (2) draft or revise critically for intellectual content; (3) approve the version to be published; and (4) agree to be accountable for all aspects of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publisher does not prescribe exact contributions that warrant authorship; follow field-specific guidelines where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosures_and_declarations_for_authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors should include information regarding sources of funding, financial or non-financial interests, ethics approval for human/animal research, informed consent, and statement on welfare of animals if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision on inclusion depends on scope of journal and article; include appropriate disclosures for work with public health or welfare implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role_and_responsibilities_of_corresponding_author
rubrics_metrics.description: One author is assigned as Corresponding Author and acts on behalf of all co-authors and ensures that questions related to accuracy or integrity are appropriately addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding Author responsibilities include ensuring all listed authors approved manuscript and order, managing communication between Journal and co-authors (may delegate to Contact/Submitting Author), providing transparency on re-use of material and making sure disclosures and data statements from all authors are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author_contribution_statements_and_CRedit_taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible include contribution statements specifying the contribution of every author. Examples provided include free-text statements and the CRediT taxonomy (Conceptualization, Methodology, Formal analysis, Writing - original draft, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For review articles where discrete statements are less applicable, state who had the idea, who performed literature search and data analysis, and who drafted or critically revised the work. For theses-based articles student usually listed as principal author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affiliation_and_author_name_policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary affiliation should be the institution where the majority of the work was done. If an author has moved, the current address may additionally be stated. Author names will be published exactly as they appear on the accepted submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes to authorship (adding/deleting authors or sequence changes) are not accepted after acceptance. Adding/deleting at revision stage generally not permitted but may be warranted with detailed explanation and Editor-in-Chief approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author_identification_and_ORCID_recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are recommended to use their ORCID ID when submitting or acquire one via the submission process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For deceased or incapacitated authors include approval from a legal representative if including them as authors is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship_disputes_and_confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of authorship dispute during peer review or after acceptance, the Journal will not adjudicate and authors will be asked to resolve the dispute themselves. If unable, Journal may withdraw manuscript or raise issue with authors' institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should treat all communication with the Journal as confidential (correspondence with editors and reviewers' reports) unless explicit consent to share has been received.
